name: THE MAN ON THE LANDING
note: A STORY ANCHOR: there is always a man on the landing, and he has not moved. RESTAGED TWICE, and the second time is the one that mattered. First from 1382,168 -- the separation plan's zone -- where his hat was cut off by the top of the frame. Then from 1350,212, where the LIVE ROOM showed what a composite sheet had not: he was standing on the STRINGER, the diagonal rail of the flight, with nothing under his boots. THERE IS NO FLAT LANDING IN THIS PLATE. The flight runs up and out of frame behind the upper wall, so the highest place a man can stand is a tread near the top of the visible run: the tread front edges are y 395, 370, 345, 320, 300, 278, 255, 235 going up, and at 235 the tread spans x 1290-1450. He stands at 1305,235, on the tread's own surface at the wall side, with 67 px of headroom. His stature is 0.74 because his feet are not on this room's floor and the engine clamps to the far height there.
poseNote: standing on the landing at the head of the stairs, hat at his side, looking at nothing

sprite.note: PHASE 2A: one frame, and that is the phase, not an omission. Static staging first, and Tyler accepts the face in the room before any life is animated on it -- doc 36 Q128. The sheet is pre-scaled to the height this room asks for where the character stands, so the engine draws it at about 1:1 instead of shrinking a 1200 px painting on every frame.

barksNote: NONE. These nine are the room's population, not its dialogue: doc 07's reputation barks belong to the named ambient cast, and nothing in Tyler's Phase 2A ruling gives a generic patron a line. No written content is invented for them here or anywhere.
